author: OpenAxolotl maintainer via the project's hero generator
tool: Blender 4.0.2 headless, tools/blender/make_axolotl.py (deterministic), then rigged by tools/rig_model.py. The mesh is built from ONE branching edge skeleton per role inflated by a skin modifier plus subdivision, so limbs and toes are branches of the body's own surface rather than separate tubes joined to it; the gill plumes are built directly in bmesh as three rami a side, each a long bare stalk carrying a feathered blade on its outer half, the three stalks aimed forward-up, out-up and back-up so three flat feathers make a three-dimensional plume; the dorsal and ventral tail membranes are gill-role pieces so they wear the translucent material rather than opaque skin. One continuous surface per role (skin, eye, gleam, gill, detail) with named axolotl_<role> materials and vertex-colour albedo. Rigging adds a 12-bone skeleton with weights from inverse-square distance to the two nearest bones, the eye and its highlight bound whole to the head, and six animation clips (idle, waddle, swim, hop, fall, hurt). 34,392 triangles, inside the character budget of 60,000.; surface maps computed by tools/blender/bake_hero_maps.py (Blender 4.0.2 headless: Smart UV Project on the shipped mesh, tangent-space normal and neutral detail maps rasterised from a deterministic procedural height field at 1024 px)
prompt: Matched against the maintainer's own reference sheet, reference/hero/01_hero_perspective.png, which they supplied and then explicitly chose over the realistic-salamander reading an earlier build followed. The reference is a stylized-cute axolotl at high craft, and the choice was made knowing it pulls against their earlier "face doesn't look cartoonish": LARGE round glossy eyes with a bright catchlight, a soft domed skull rather than a flat wedge, a gentle upturned mouth seam, three long bare gill stalks a side carrying feathered blades held up and clear of the head, a broad translucent tail fin, and discrete pink blotches over the head and back. What survives from the realistic pass, because it was never in tension with the reference: limbs and toes grown as branches of one edge skeleton so every join is continuous flesh, four toes in front and five behind, a laterally compressed tail blade, and a dorsal crest that swells over the tail rather than running flat along the spine. SUPERSEDES the original upload, a glb from an uncommitted AI-written trimesh script: 85 welded primitives with no generator in the repo. The uploaded reference package's own glb was verified byte-identical to that original upload, so the sheet's textured model was never available as a file; this generator builds the animal in vertex-coloured geometry instead. The skin palette leans WARM on purpose — the shared lighting rig's sky ambient is blue, so a colour balanced in isolation renders lavender. Skin surface maps (axolotl_skin_normal.png, axolotl_skin_detail.png): pore-scale relief over soft mottle bumps and a neutral tonal mottle, both computed from seeded value noise over object-space position so they are exactly reproducible and continuous across UV island seams.
